title: Xcode Derived Data
explain: Build products and indexes Xcode keeps per project. Xcode rebuilds them the next time you open or build the project; the first build afterwards takes longer.

title: Xcode device support files
explain: Debug symbols copied from a device OS version you have not used for 90 days. Xcode copies them again when you next connect a device running that version.

title: Old Xcode archives
explain: App builds you archived more than six months ago. Keep the ones for releases you still support: their debug symbols are needed to read crash reports.

title: SwiftUI preview data
explain: Simulator data behind Xcode's SwiftUI previews. Xcode recreates it the next time a preview runs.

title: Simulators unused for 90 days
explain: A simulated device nobody has booted for 90 days, with the apps and data installed on it. Xcode can create a fresh one; running xcrun simctl delete unavailable removes the ones for runtimes you no longer have.

title: Simulator caches
explain: Shared caches the simulators build on first launch. They are rebuilt the next time a simulator starts.

title: App caches unused for 30 days
explain: Files an app saved to speed itself up and has not touched for 30 days. The app downloads or rebuilds what it needs; it may be a little slower the first time. Apple's own caches are left alone.

title: Sandboxed app caches unused for 30 days
explain: The cache folder of an App Store or sandboxed app, untouched for 30 days. The app recreates it as needed. Apple's own apps are left alone.

title: Old logs
explain: Diagnostic logs apps and macOS wrote more than 30 days ago. They are only needed when investigating an old problem. Some in /Library/Logs need an administrator to remove.

title: Items in the Trash
explain: Files you already moved to the Trash still take space until it is emptied. Empty it in the Finder when you are sure; StorageLens never empties it, because that is what makes its own deletions undoable.

title: Old installers in Downloads
explain: Disk images, installer packages and archives downloaded more than 90 days ago. Once an app is installed its installer is usually not needed; a zip may hold documents, so check those.

title: Downloads untouched for a year
explain: Files in Downloads that nothing has changed for over a year. Many are one-off downloads, but this folder often holds documents too, so look before removing.

title: iPhone and iPad backups
explain: Local backups of an iPhone or iPad. If the device is backed up to iCloud, or you no longer have it, an old backup may not be needed; otherwise it is the only copy of that device's data.

title: Mail attachments
explain: Attachments Mail has downloaded. StorageLens does not touch Mail's own folders; to reclaim this space, remove attachments from within Mail or change how much mail it keeps offline.

title: Opened Mail attachments
explain: Copies Mail made when you opened an attachment more than 30 days ago. The attachment itself stays in the message, so Mail can make a new copy.

title: Docker disk image
explain: One sparse file holding every Docker image, container and volume; its real size on disk is usually far below its apparent size. Removing it would delete all of them, so StorageLens never offers to. Run docker system prune (see docker system df) to reclaim space inside it.

title: Homebrew download cache
explain: Packages Homebrew downloaded to install or upgrade. It downloads them again if needed; brew cleanup does the same job.

title: npm package cache
explain: Every package npm has downloaded. npm fetches what a project needs again on its next install.

title: Document versions
explain: Earlier versions of documents, kept by macOS for Browse All Versions. macOS manages and trims this space itself.

title: Swap and sleep image
explain: Virtual memory and the copy of memory written when the Mac sleeps. macOS sizes these as it needs; they shrink after a restart.
